target_customer: Independent behavioral health clinicians and practices, and insurers
problem: Clinicians lose time to documentation and run on fragmented practice software, and mental health care delivery is analog.
business_model: Free EHR software for practices (free up to 20 team members per site) converting into a clinical group billing insurers
product_category: Behavioral health EHR and medical group

founders.name: Amie Leighton
founders.background_notes: Profile also lists a student society role, not a company.

founders.name: Saroosh Khan
founders.background_notes: Profile cites an ARC-AGI-2 score; employers and education not listed.

competitors.name: SimplePractice
competitors.what: Dominant practice management EHR with AI note add on

competitors.name: Blueprint
competitors.what: Free EHR with per session AI notes

technical_complexity.rationale: HIPAA EHR with AI documentation, billing and prescribing; the care delivery side is operational.

defensibility.rationale: EHR data and insurer contracts create lock in, but software features are copyable.

market_need_then: Clinician administrative burden is large; Allia reports reducing it by up to 80 percent (company claim in press).

brand_strength.rationale: Clean name but limited press; similar Allia Health Group exists.

outcome_analysis: Allia Health is a Summer 2026 company that uses free practice software as a wedge into a clinical group. No outcome yet: the company is Active and a 2026 batch member; outcome searches found no acquisition, shutdown or layoff news. The site reports thousands of clinicians, but inconsistent figures (8,000 versus 7,000) and unverified insurance claims limit confidence.
notes: Press article (2025-05) names four investors in a most recent round without amount or stage, so the stage is recorded as other. FundedIQ lists a $2.0M seed in 2025-06, unverified. The $50M annualized insurance contract figure is a company claim.
